questions.question: Describe the Weimar constitution and explain two features that made the republic unstable.
questions.expected_answer: Germany became a democratic republic in 1919 with votes for all men and women over 20, a Reichstag elected by proportional representation, a chancellor responsible to the Reichstag, an elected president and guaranteed freedoms. Proportional representation produced many parties and unstable coalition governments; Article 48 allowed the president to rule by decree in an emergency, bypassing parliament. It was also attacked by communists and nationalists and blamed for the defeat and the treaty.

questions.question: Explain the terms of the Treaty of Versailles under the headings land, army, money and blame, and show how one term affected South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Land: about 13 percent of European territory and 10 percent of the population lost; Alsace-Lorraine to France, Polish Corridor to Poland, Saar under the League, all colonies taken as mandates. Army: 100 000 volunteers, no tanks, aircraft or submarines, six battleships, Rhineland demilitarised. Money: reparations of 132 billion gold marks. Blame: Article 231, the War Guilt Clause. German South West Africa became a League of Nations mandate administered by South Africa.

questions.question: Explain why Germans resented the treaty and how the stab-in-the-back myth and the hyperinflation of 1923 weakened support for the Weimar Republic.
questions.expected_answer: Germany was excluded from negotiations, believed it had not been beaten, and found the war guilt, losses of land and reparations humiliating. The myth that the army had been betrayed by socialists, Jews and democratic politicians blamed the republic for defeat. In 1923, after the Ruhr occupation, the government printed money and hyperinflation destroyed savings and pensions, turning the middle class against the republic.
